question: Does the inference-time null for non-chain context triples (arxiv:2609.10237) replicate when the same contrast is used as a fine-tuning signal, or does training extract value from passage-coherent context that prompting cannot?
description: arxiv:2609.10237 holds the triple count fixed and reports that replacing every non-chain triple with material from an unrelated entity neighbourhood changes answer accuracy by +0.003 F1 (removing the chain is what hurts). The idea's premise is that non-chain triples drawn from the same source passage provide supportive context during training. The two claims are in tension, though not strictly contradictory because 2609 is an inference-time prompting study on frozen LLMs over 125 questions, whereas the idea proposes fine-tuning. The key unknown is whether gradient updates can exploit passage-coherent context that a prompt cannot, or whether the null will replicate for training.
confidence_basis: Based on a full-text reading of a directly targeted paper with reported per-hop numbers, tempered because it is a single preprint on synthetic biomedical multiple-choice QA without a token-matched distractor control.
rationale: If the null replicates under fine-tuning, the idea's central mechanism is unsupported and the contribution collapses to the (already-occupied) subgraph-retrieval space; if it does not, the idea has a genuine, cheap-to-test claim.
resolution: The inference-time null does not straightforwardly replicate under fine-tuning. arxiv:2609.12230 fine-tunes Qwen3-14B under exactly the contested contrast (KG-grounded: target triple/path only; CG-grounded: target plus same-source-chunk supporting triples) with matched base model, LoRA setup, optimizer, sequence length, batch size, epochs, learning-rate schedule and equal QA-item counts, and reports that the context-augmented model beats the KG-only model in every disease, evaluation setting and hop length, by 1.98/2.20/2.15 points on Gastroparesis 3/4/5-hop and 1.50-2.66 points for Diabetes. So training does appear to extract value that prompting did not, and the 'premise is false' inference is weakened. What remains open is attribution: the two regimes have equal example counts but the CG examples contain more context tokens, and no token-matched random-distractor control was run, so the gain could still be partly a context-volume or question-distribution effect rather than passage coherence.
